merged.title: fix(port/rac1-ntsc): bind moby updates to the US class update table
merged.author: mateuszklysz
merged.untrustedBody:
The warm savestate change (12342e62) runs assign_moby_class_data as host C (rac1/host/moby_class.c), written against PAL's addresses and mapped per version through RAC1_ADDR. For the US build it mapped PAL's update table (0x1B3900, resident_moby_class_data) to 0x1B3900 as well, but the US decomp's update table is D_001B3580: the three slot tables (resources, updates, class ids) are each 0x380 lower than PAL's, and the US 0x1B3900 is the s16 class ids register_moby_class writes.

So every class's update went into the class id table, and the table init_moby_instance copies a moby's update (+0x74) from stayed zero: on NTSC-U no moby updated (nothing moved, crates could not be broken) and the class ids were overwritten (bolts drawn at the wrong size).

Verified: rac1-ntsc's own decomp (assign_moby_class_data.c, init_moby_instance.c, moby_class_tables.h) names the tables at these addresses; Not built or run in the game here (no disc in the container).

merged.title: fix(port): a skipped frame drops its effect texture notes too
merged.author: mateuszklysz
merged.untrustedBody:
When the port skips a frame to catch up, it cleared the tick's effect quads and their uploads but kept effect_texture_ids, the notes effect_quad makes for quads with an 8-bit texture and a CLUT of their own. The next frame's effect_textures() read them against the new tick's quads: an index past the list, a garbage upload index and a SIGSEGV in clut_csm1 (rac1-ntsc on Android, loading a save on Oltanis).

The skip clears effect_texture_ids, effect_hashed and effect_sources with the quads, and effect_textures() skips a note whose quad or upload is out of range.

The log printed garbage after each level pair map's "for <caller>" line and the session's start time: libc++'s std::format formats a whole char array, past its NUL. Both are formatted as C strings now, and a caller that was not found is not logged.

merged.title: fix(rac1): the camera follows the ship as it leaves a planet
merged.author: mateuszklysz
merged.untrustedBody:

When Ratchet takes off, once the take-off scene ends and the ship flies away from the planet
(SpaceFlightUpdate, `func_00230A90` on PAL / `FUN_0022f778` on NTSC-U, state 3), the camera sat in the
wrong place and did not move. This happened on every planet, on PAL and NTSC-U alike.

The camera is placed and moves the way the console has it: it blends from the level's source camera

## How

State 3 drives the camera through two of the executable's empty hook stubs: `func_001E9770` (set up
from the camera's position, once, as the state starts) and `func_001E9778` (the blended position,
every frame). Each level's program fills those stubs with its own functions, the same way it fills
`func_001E9780` (the blended rotation, the next call). hostgen's `level_hooks` already routed
`func_001E9780` and the other hooks to the loaded level's function, but these two were missing. The
port therefore ran the empty stub

Near miss for `func_002DE618` (212 bytes, boot + 27 levels): 212/212 bytes, 0/28 places. It replaces the 188-byte draft from 2414789a.

The function looks up a key in the five-entry chunk table at `D_001B1F50`. If the entry has flag 2 set, it clears flag 4 and calls `func_002B7AD0` when the byte at `D_001F2840 + 0xDB` is set. It then clears flag 2 and returns 0.

## What still differs

Every instruction matches retail except the registers of the two reduced table pointers. Retail walks the keys in `$a1` and the flags in `$a2`, and the loop ends on the keys pointer. This source swaps the two pointers, which gives 10 differing lines.

- Indexing with `i * 2` keeps the `$s2` byte offset and the base for the final `&= ~2` separate from the flags walk. Pointer walks merge them, which is why the old draft was 188 bytes.
